item.base_system: AlNbTiVZr 0.25 high-entropy alloy (homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h)
item.intervention: Oxidation testing at 600 °C for 100 h in static lab air
item.processing: Specimens placed in alumina crucibles, oxidized at 600 °C for 100 h
item.structure_change: Surface layer consisted of V2O5, VO2, TiO2, Nb2O5, and TiNb2O7 oxides; oxide scale thickness 15–30 μm with multiple cracks nucleating at the scale-metal interface
item.property_change: Specific mass gain of 7.2 mg/cm² after 100 h
item.attributed_mechanism: Breakaway oxidation induced by spallation of the oxide scale due to nucleation of voluminous Nb2O5 and TiNb2O7 oxides
quotes: At 600–700 °C, two-stage oxidation kinetics was found: Nearly parabolic oxidation (n = 0.46–0.48) at the first stage, transitioned to breakaway oxidation (n = 0.75–0.72) at the second stage.
The surface layer at 600 °C consisted of the V 2 O 5 , VO 2 , TiO 2 , Nb 2 O 5 , and TiNb 2 O 7 oxides.
The specific mass gains were estimated to be 7.2, 38.1, and 107.5, and 225.5 mg/cm 2 at 600, 700, and 800 °C for 100 h, and 900 °C for 50 h, respectively.

item.base_system: AlNbTiVZr 0.25 alloy oxidized at 600 °C for 0.5 h
item.intervention: Extended oxidation time to 100 h at 600 °C
item.processing: Oxidation in static lab air at 600 °C for 100 h
item.structure_change: Initial TiO2 and VO2 oxides replaced by V2O5, TiNb2O7, and Nb2O5; B2 phase peaks vanished; fine whisker-like oxides (~500 nm) formed
item.property_change: Specific mass gain increased from initial stage to 7.2 mg/cm² at 100 h
item.attributed_mechanism: Acceleration of oxidation due to whisker-like morphology of V-rich oxides accelerating oxygen ingress and nucleation of Nb2O5 and TiNb2O7
quotes: At 600 °C, the alloy demonstrated nearly parabolic kinetics (n = 0.46) in the range of 0–20 h but then the oxidation rate increased significantly (n = 0.75).
Starting from 5 h exposure, tiny peaks of the V 2 O 5 , TiNb 2 O 7 , and Nb 2 O 5 oxides were found.
After 20 h, the Braggs peaks of the B2 phase vanished.

item.base_system: AlNbTiVZr 0.25 alloy oxidized at 800 °C for 0.5 h
item.intervention: Extended oxidation time to 100 h at 800 °C
item.processing: Oxidation in static lab air at 800 °C for 100 h
item.structure_change: Elimination of TiO2 oxide and B2 phase from diffraction patterns; whisker size increased to ~1.5 μm; surface enriched with V and O initially, then with Al, Nb, V, Ti
item.property_change: Specific mass gain reached 107.5 mg/cm² at 100 h
item.attributed_mechanism: Formation of thick, porous oxide scale with enhanced ingress of gaseous species due to V-rich oxide evaporation
quotes: At 800 °C, a fairly rapid (n = 0.78) oxidation rate was observed throughout the entire duration of testing.
Increasing in time over 5 h resulted in the elimination of both the TiO 2 oxide and the B2 phase from the diffraction patterns.
The specific mass gains were estimated to be 7.2, 38.1, and 107.5, and 225.5 mg/cm 2 at 600, 700, and 800 °C for 100 h, and 900 °C for 50 h, respectively.

item.base_system: AlNbTiVZr 0.25 alloy oxidized at 600 °C for 100 h
item.intervention: Analysis of cross-sectional morphology and composition
item.processing: SEM-BSE imaging and EDS mapping of cross-sections
item.structure_change: Oxide scale 15–30 μm thick with cracks; external (V, Zr)-rich layer, inner (Ti, Nb, Al)-rich layer; wide single-phase zone below scale with fine pores
item.attributed_mechanism: Cracks nucleate on scale-metal interface and propagate towards surface due to stresses from Nb2O5 and TiNb2O7 formation
quotes: The thickness of the oxide scale varied from ~15 μm to ~30 μm ( Figure 6 a).
Multiple cracks in the oxide scale were found; the cracks seemed to nucleate on the scale-metal interface and propagated towards the surface ( Figure 6 a).
Under the oxide scale, a wide (~100–150 μm) single-phase zone of the substrate with a homogeneous distribution of the constitutive elements was found.

item.base_system: AlNbTiVZr 0.25 alloy oxidized at 800 °C for 100 h
item.intervention: Analysis of cross-sectional morphology and composition
item.processing: SEM-BSE imaging and EDS mapping of cross-sections
item.structure_change: Oxide scale ~800 μm thick with complex structure: top whisker layer, needle-shaped (Zr, Nb)-rich particles, Ti/V-rich zones with pores, Nb2Zr6O17 particle layers
item.attributed_mechanism: Oxidation front ascended along Zr5Al3 particles; Zr-rich particles dissolved forming Nb2Zr6O17; pores formed at former particle sites
quotes: At 800 °C, the oxide scale was significantly thicker (~800 μm) and had a complex structure ( Figure 7 a).

A close examination of the transition zone (#2 in Figure 7 a,c) revealed some notable features. The oxidation front ascended easily along the Zr 5 Al 3 particles but was slightly impeded by the B2 phase.
Further, as the oxidation front progressed, Zr-rich particles tended to dissolve with the subsequent formation of the Nb 2 Zr 6 O 17 oxide particles on the borders of their previous location.

item.intervention: Comparison of surface composition with 800 °C oxidation
item.structure_change: At 600 °C: surface enriched with V and O; At 800 °C: nearly equal concentrations of Al, Nb, V, Ti and high O content
item.attributed_mechanism: Different oxidation mechanisms leading to different surface chemistries
quotes: The surface of the sample after 100 h at 600 °C was enriched with V and O, while, nearly equal concentrations of Al, Nb, V, and Ti, and a high O content were found after oxidation at 800 °C ( Table 3 ).
After 100 h of oxidation at 600 °C, fine whisker-like oxides with the average transversal size of ~500 nm were found at the surface ( Figure 5 c).
Similar oxide morphology was observed after oxidation at 800 °C ( Figure 5 d). However, the average transversal size of whiskers was ~1.5 μm.

item.processing: Literature comparison of specific mass gains
item.property_change: Mass gains of AlNbTiZr RHEA are ~5–12 times lower than AlNbTiVZr 0.25 alloy
item.attributed_mechanism: V is largely responsible for the poor oxidation resistance of the AlNbTiVZr 0.25 alloy
quotes: Particularly, the mass gain of the V-free AlNbTiZr RHEA at 600–800 °C is ~5–12 times lower than that of the AlNbTiVZr 0.25 alloy.
This finding confirms that V is largely responsible for the poor oxidation resistance of the AlNbTiVZr 0.25 alloy.
The mass gains of the AlNbTiVZr 0.25 alloy are comparable with some of the V-based alloys, namely V-30Al [ [59] ], Ti-based and TiAl-based alloys with a high V content

item.intervention: Comparison with Inconel 690 and TiAl alloys
item.processing: Literature comparison of specific mass gains
item.property_change: Mass gains of Inconel 690 or orthorhombic (Ti2AlNb) and gamma (TiAl) alloys are lower by 3 or 2 orders of magnitude, respectively
quotes: In turn, the mass gains of Inconel 690 or orthorhombic (Ti 2 AlNb) and gamma (TiAl) alloys after oxidation at 800 °C are lower than the experimentally observed values by 3 or 2 orders of magnitude, respectively ( Table 4 ).
In general, the obtained results demonstrate that despite its promising mechanical properties, the AlNbTiVZr 0.25 alloy shows rather poor oxidation resistance.
This can obviously limit the potential applications of the alloy.
